system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Paris, France. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Paris itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Paris space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Marais, Saint-Germain, Avenue Matignon/8th, Belleville/Pantin) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Paris spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Paris, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.note: France's biggest home-grown mega-gallery, with global outposts; launched Murakami, Sophie Calle, JR and Kaws in Europe and anchors the Marais scene.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac
galleries.address_hint: 7 rue Debelleyme (plus a vast space in Pantin)
galleries.note: Blue-chip programme (Baselitz, Kiefer, Rauschenberg estate, Warhol) split between an intimate Marais townhouse and a museum-scale Pantin hangar.

galleries.name: Kamel Mennour
galleries.address_hint: 47 rue Saint-André-des-Arts / 6 rue du Pont de Lodi
galleries.note: The most institutionally connected French gallery of its generation: Anish Kapoor, Camille Henrot, Lee Ufan, Latifa Echakhch, Tadashi Kawamata.

galleries.name: Galerie Chantal Crousel
galleries.note: Since 1980 a benchmark for conceptual and international rigour: Gonzalez-Foerster, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Mona Hatoum, Wolfgang Tillmans, Danh Vo.

galleries.name: Marian Goodman Gallery
galleries.note: Paris arm of the legendary New York dealer; Gerhard Richter, Steve McQueen, Tacita Dean, William Kentridge, Annette Messager.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.address_hint: 4 rue de Ponthieu (plus 9 rue de Castiglione)
galleries.note: Two Paris spaces from the world's most powerful dealer, driving the 8th arrondissement's revival around Art Basel Paris.

galleries.name: David Zwirner
galleries.note: Opened 2019 and immediately central to Paris's internationalisation; shows Kerry James Marshall, Wolfgang Tillmans, Raymond Pettibon, Njideka Akunyili Crosby.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth
galleries.note: Its 2023 Paris flagship brought Louise Bourgeois, Mark Bradford, Pipilotti Rist and a major estate programme to the Golden Triangle.

galleries.name: Templon
galleries.address_hint: 30 rue Beaubourg / 28 rue du Grenier Saint-Lazare
galleries.note: Founded 1966, the historic Paris gallery for American and European painting; Kehinde Wiley, Chiharu Shiota, Omar Ba, Jitish Kallat.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: International network gallery mixing Picasso estate scholarship with a strong figurative-painting roster.

galleries.name: Palais de Tokyo
galleries.note: Europe's largest kunsthalle: no collection, all emerging and mid-career commissions; the single most influential non-commercial platform in Paris.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galleries.address_hint: 57 rue du Temple (and 46 rue Vieille du Temple)
galleries.note: Berlin dealer's Paris spaces; Albert Oehlen, Bridget Riley, Camille Henrot, Rebecca Warren, top-tier fair presence.

galleries.name: Galerie Lelong & Co.
galleries.note: Historic house with a publishing arm; Jaume Plensa, Kiki Smith, Barthélémy Toguo, plus major estates (Tàpies, Bacon prints).

galleries.name: Galerie Nathalie Obadia
galleries.address_hint: 3 rue du Cloître Saint-Merri / 18 rue du Bourg-Tibourg
galleries.note: Two Marais spaces and Brussels; Fiona Rae, Josep Grau-Garriga estate, Andres Serrano, Youssef Nabil, Laure Prouvost.

galleries.name: Air de Paris
galleries.address_hint: 43 rue de la Commune de Paris, Romainville
galleries.note: Cult 1990s gallery of the relational-aesthetics generation (Gonzalez-Foerster, Parreno, Gillick, Trecartin); a taste-setter for three decades.

galleries.name: White Cube
galleries.note: London powerhouse's 2023 Paris space; Tracey Emin, Julie Mehretu, Theaster Gates and a strong estates programme.

galleries.name: Esther Schipper
galleries.note: Berlin gallery of Philippe Parreno, Ryan Gander and Ann Veronica Janssens; its Vendôme space is one of the most watched recent arrivals.

galleries.name: Lafayette Anticipations
galleries.note: Galeries Lafayette foundation in an OMA-rebuilt warehouse: production-based commissions that have launched many careers.

galleries.name: Galleria Continua
galleries.note: San Gimignano-born international gallery; Kader Attia, JR, Anish Kapoor, Pascale Marthine Tayou, with a strong Global South emphasis.

galleries.name: gb agency
galleries.note: Curator's gallery par excellence, rediscovering historical conceptualists alongside Ryan Gander, Omer Fast and Pratchaya Phinthong.

galleries.name: Galerie Jocelyn Wolff
galleries.address_hint: 43 rue de la Commune de Paris, Romainville
galleries.note: Research-driven programme (Franz Erhard Walther, Katinka Bock, Prinz Gholam) with sustained museum crossover.

galleries.name: Galerie Georges-Philippe & Nathalie Vallois
galleries.note: Nouveaux Réalistes estates plus Gilles Barbier, Alain Bublex and Boris Achour; a Saint-Germain institution since 1990.

galleries.name: Galerie Karsten Greve
galleries.note: Cy Twombly, Louise Bourgeois, Pierrette Bloch and Gideon Rubin in a grand Marais space; Cologne-based, decades of Paris presence.

galleries.name: Jeanne Bucher Jaeger
galleries.note: Founded 1925, one of Europe's oldest continuously run galleries; Dubuffet and Vieira da Silva history alongside Susumu Shingu and Miquel Barceló.

galleries.name: Xippas
galleries.note: International network (Geneva, Montevideo, Punta del Este); Vera Molnár, Dan Walsh, Farah Atassi, Valérie Jouve.

galleries.name: Galerie Michel Rein
galleries.note: Politically engaged programme; Jimmie Durham estate, Raphaël Zarka, Chourouk Hriech, Didier Marcel, with Brussels space.

galleries.name: Balice Hertling
galleries.note: Emerged from Belleville as the key discovery gallery of the 2010s (Camille Blatrix, Isabelle Cornaro, Neïl Beloufa).

galleries.name: Crèvecœur
galleries.note: Sharp young programme with international traction; Puppies Puppies, Anne Bourse, Ghislaine Leung-adjacent artists, strong fair record.

galleries.name: High Art
galleries.note: Influential post-internet-era gallery; Bri Williams, Nicolas Ceccaldi, Rachel Rossin, with a second space in Arles.

galleries.name: Galerie Sultana
galleries.note: Guillaume Sultana's queer- and body-focused programme; Louise Sartor, Alex Foxton, Jesse Darling-adjacent circles.

galleries.name: Marcelle Alix
galleries.note: Feminist, essayistic programme run by two former curators; Charlotte Moth, Ana Jotta, Laura Lamiel.

galleries.name: In Situ – fabienne leclerc
galleries.address_hint: 43 rue de la Commune de Paris, Romainville
galleries.note: Subodh Gupta, Mark Dion, Gary Hill, Otobong Nkanga history; a pillar of the Komunuma gallery cluster.

galleries.name: Praz-Delavallade
galleries.note: Franco-American axis since 1995 (also Los Angeles); John Armleder, Amy Bessone, Jim Shaw, Bertrand Lavier.

galleries.name: Galerie Poggi
galleries.note: Jérôme Poggi's civic-minded programme; Bertille Bak, Mathieu Kleyebe Abonnenc, Josèfa Ntjam, Ann Veronica Janssens editions.

galleries.name: mor charpentier
galleries.note: Latin American and post-colonial focus; Óscar Muñoz, Teresa Margolles, Carlos Motta, Milena Bonilla.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: Chicago dealer whose Paris space is central to the visibility of African and diasporic painting (Amoako Boafo, Clotilde Jiménez).

galleries.name: Skarstedt
galleries.note: Secondary-market heavyweight (Prince, Sherman, Condo, Kippenberger) whose Paris opening signalled the Matignon boom.

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo
galleries.note: Milan gallery's single-work vitrine format; a compact but highly visible Paris presence for a top international roster.

galleries.name: Mendes Wood DM
galleries.note: São Paulo gallery whose Paris space brought Paulo Nazareth, Sonia Gomes and Lucas Arruda to a European audience.

galleries.name: Kadist
galleries.note: Collection-backed foundation with residencies and a research-led exhibition programme linking Paris and San Francisco.

galleries.name: Peter Freeman, Inc.
galleries.note: New York dealer's Paris space; minimal and conceptual classics (Mel Bochner, Thomas Schütte, Catherine Murphy).

galleries.name: Galerie frank elbaz
galleries.note: Rediscoveries of Gutai, Davide Balula and Sheila Hicks-era historical figures alongside young conceptualists.

galleries.name: Loevenbruck
galleries.note: Irreverent French programme; Présence Panchounette estate, Philippe Mayaux, Peter Saul, Gina Pane archive.

galleries.name: Galerie Christophe Gaillard
galleries.note: Estates (Michel Journiac, Martin Barré-era figures) plus contemporary photography and performance; also a Brussels space.

galleries.name: Semiose
galleries.note: Painting-forward, funny and precise; Françoise Pétrovitch, Laurent Proux, Marion Charlet, with a busy fair calendar.

galleries.name: Fondation d'entreprise Pernod Ricard
galleries.note: Its annual prize exhibition is the key barometer of the emerging French scene; free, curator-led programme.

galleries.name: Le Plateau – Frac Île-de-France
galleries.note: The regional collection's Paris kunsthalle, a long-standing platform for first institutional shows.

galleries.name: Galerie Suzanne Tarasieve
galleries.note: Champion of German and Eastern European painting in Paris (Baselitz circle, Boris Mikhailov, Marlene Dumas-adjacent figures).

galleries.name: Galerie Anne-Sarah Bénichou
galleries.note: Politically alert programme with strong institutional placement; Enrique Ramírez, Mounir Fatmi, Randa Maroufi.

galleries.name: Ciaccia Levi
galleries.note: Paris-Milan gallery born of Antoine Levi's; incisive young international roster and consistent fair presence.

galleries.name: Sans titre
galleries.note: One of the most watched younger Paris galleries, showing emerging international artists with a curatorial edge.

galleries.name: Édouard Montassut
galleries.note: Small, critically outsized apartment-scale gallery central to the Paris-Berlin-Brussels emerging network.

galleries.name: Galerie Allen
galleries.note: Anglophone-founded gallery with a conceptual, cross-generational programme and steady international fair presence.

galleries.name: Galerie Papillon
galleries.note: Long-running Marais gallery known for drawing, sculpture and loyal support of mid-career French artists.

galleries.name: Galerie Anne Barrault
galleries.note: Drawing, comics-adjacent and outsider-inflected practices; a distinctive, critically respected niche.

galleries.name: Galerie Thomas Bernard – Cortex Athletico
galleries.note: Bordeaux-born gallery now in Paris; conceptual and post-minimal French artists with regular museum crossovers.

galleries.name: Galerie Laurent Godin
galleries.note: Wide-ranging programme from Wang Du and Delphine Coindet to international pop-conceptual figures.

galleries.name: Galerie Eric Dupont
galleries.note: Thirty-year Marais fixture with a painting- and photography-based French and international roster.

galleries.name: Galerie Les Filles du Calvaire
galleries.note: Leading Paris gallery for contemporary photography and image-based practice; strong Paris Photo presence.

galleries.name: Polka Galerie
galleries.note: Photography gallery and magazine; documentary heavyweights alongside contemporary photographers.

galleries.name: Magnin-A
galleries.note: André Magnin's gallery, pivotal for African contemporary art in Europe (Seydou Keïta, Chéri Samba, Omar Victor Diop).

galleries.name: Galerie Cécile Fakhoury
galleries.note: Abidjan-founded gallery whose Paris space anchors a strong West African contemporary roster.

galleries.name: Bétonsalon – Centre d'art et de recherche
galleries.note: University-embedded art centre with rigorous research, decolonial and pedagogical programming.

galleries.name: Le BAL
galleries.note: Independent space for the document image — photography, film, video — with an influential publishing and education arm.

galleries.name: Galerie Jean Fournier
galleries.note: Historic gallery of Simon Hantaï and Supports/Surfaces, still showing abstraction across generations.

galleries.name: Galerie Maeght
galleries.note: Legendary 20th-century house (Miró, Giacometti, Calder) with continuing contemporary and editions activity.

galleries.name: Galerie Claude Bernard
galleries.note: Since 1957 the Paris address for figurative drawing and sculpture; Bacon and Giacometti exhibition history.

galleries.name: Galerie Denise René
galleries.note: Founded 1944, the birthplace of kinetic and geometric abstraction (Vasarely, Soto, Agam); still programming today.

galleries.name: Applicat-Prazan
galleries.note: Reference dealer for postwar School of Paris abstraction, with scholarly catalogues and major fair booths.

galleries.name: Loeve&Co
galleries.note: Rediscovery-driven gallery reviving overlooked French postwar figures with exhibition-quality research.

galleries.name: Tornabuoni Art
galleries.note: Italian modern and Arte Povera specialist (Fontana, Boetti, Castellani) with a strong Paris exhibition programme.

galleries.name: Ceysson & Bénétière
galleries.note: The gallery that globalised Supports/Surfaces; international network from Saint-Étienne to New York.

galleries.name: RX&SLAG
galleries.note: Franco-American merger with a wide international roster and consistent large-scale installations.

galleries.name: Backslash
galleries.note: Politically engaged mid-size gallery with a strong Middle Eastern and emerging French roster.

galleries.name: Galerie Derouillon
galleries.note: Young painting-led gallery with two Paris spaces and rapid international fair expansion.

galleries.name: Galerie Sator
galleries.address_hint: 43 rue de la Commune de Paris, Romainville
galleries.note: Founder member of the Komunuma cluster; research-based programme spanning photography, painting and installation.

galleries.name: Galerie Hussenot
galleries.note: Long-standing gallery with an international, sculpture-heavy roster and a discreet but respected programme.

galleries.name: Galerie Marguo
galleries.note: Fast-rising young gallery bridging Paris, Asia and the US with a painting-focused emerging roster.

galleries.name: Christian Berst art brut
galleries.note: The world reference for art brut and outsider art, with museum-grade scholarship and touring exhibitions.

galleries.name: Galerie Alberta Pane
galleries.note: Paris-Venice gallery with a process- and material-driven international programme.

galleries.name: mfc-michèle didier
galleries.note: Publisher-gallery of conceptual art multiples; essential for artists' books and editions (Weiner, Kosuth, Broodthaers heirs).

galleries.name: Galerie Jean Brolly
galleries.note: Rigorous abstraction and radical painting; a quiet reference point for French geometric and analytic practice.

galleries.name: Galerie Anne de Villepoix
galleries.note: Since the late 1980s an early supporter of international conceptual and photographic artists in Paris.

galleries.name: Galerie Dominique Fiat
galleries.note: Established Marais gallery with a photography- and installation-based French roster.

galleries.name: Fitzpatrick Gallery
galleries.note: Robbie Fitzpatrick's Paris gallery, a hub for a transatlantic younger generation and critical group shows.

galleries.name: Galerie Chloé Salgado
galleries.note: Emerging-focused gallery with a sharp international programme and growing fair visibility.

galleries.name: Galerie Valeria Cetraro
galleries.note: Young gallery known for careful, essayistic solo shows by emerging French and international artists.

galleries.name: Galerie VU'
galleries.note: Agency-born photography gallery, a key Paris platform for contemporary documentary and author photography.

galleries.name: Galerie Natalie Seroussi
galleries.note: Surrealist and avant-garde specialist who pairs historic material with contemporary interventions.

galleries.name: Jousse Entreprise
galleries.note: Contemporary art alongside a celebrated modern design activity; long-standing Marais presence.

galleries.name: Treize
galleries.note: Artist- and curator-run space with an experimental, discursive programme influential well beyond its size.

galleries.name: DOC!
galleries.note: Artist-run occupation of a former school: studios, exhibitions and concerts, a key node of the young Paris scene.

galleries.name: Glassbox
galleries.note: One of the oldest artist-run spaces in Paris (est. 1997), a training ground for generations of artists and curators.

galleries.name: La Générale
galleries.note: Self-managed cooperative of artists and researchers, with exhibitions, residencies and performance.

galleries.name: Point Éphémère
galleries.note: Canal-side centre for dynamic art production: residencies, exhibitions and a long-running emerging-art programme.

galleries.name: Villa Belleville
galleries.note: City-supported residency and exhibition space at the heart of the Belleville artist community.

galleries.name: Cité internationale des arts
galleries.note: Vast international residency programme with public open studios and exhibitions; a first Paris foothold for many artists.

galleries.name: Fondation Fiminco
galleries.address_hint: 43 rue de la Commune de Paris, Romainville
galleries.note: Residency campus and exhibition halls anchoring the Romainville gallery cluster on the Paris periphery.

galleries.name: Poush
galleries.note: Huge artist-studio complex with public exhibitions; a magnet for collectors and curators during Paris art week.

galleries.name: Le CENTQUATRE-PARIS
galleries.note: Municipal arts centre with residencies and large-scale contemporary exhibitions reaching a wide public.
